d: Learn how to optimize concurrent API calls by letting the engine automatically batch them into fewer HTTP requests.
h:
Some APIs are capable of transparent batching, meaning the engine can automatically combine multiple concurrent API calls into fewer HTTP requests behind the scenes.

You don't need to use a different API or supply different arguments. Simply start multiple calls concurrently instead of waiting for each one to finish before starting the next.

Why use transparent batching

Many Roblox APIs communicate with backend services over HTTP and are subject to rate limits. Making many requests in a short period of time can increase latency and may cause some requests to be throttled or fail.

Transparent batching reduces the number of HTTP requests sent by the engine. Instead of sending a separate HTTP request for every API call, the engine groups nearby concurrent calls into fewer network requests automatically. This improves performance for your players and reduces the likelihood of hitting rate limits.

For example, if your code performs 20 product lookups at the same time, transparent batching can combine those calls into just one or two HTTP requests instead of sending 20 separate requests.

Use concurrent calls

Transparent batching only works when multiple calls to the same supported API are started concurrently. If each call waits for the previous one to finish, the engine sends a separate HTTP request for each call instead of batching them together.

Instead of starting calls one at a time:

-- Serial: slow, one HTTP request at a time
local MarketplaceService = game:GetService("MarketplaceService")

for _, productId in productIds do
    local info = MarketplaceService:GetProductInfoAsync(productId, Enum.InfoType.Product)
    print(info.Name)
end

Start them concurrently:

-- Concurrent: the engine combines these into fewer HTTP requests
local MarketplaceService = game:GetService("MarketplaceService")

local results = {}
local remaining = #productIds

local function fetch(productId)
    local success, info = pcall(function()
        return MarketplaceService:GetProductInfoAsync(productId, Enum.InfoType.Product)
    end)

    if success then
        results[productId] = info
    else
        warn("Failed:", productId, info)
    end

    remaining -= 1
end

for _, productId in productIds do
    task.spawn(fetch, productId)
end

while remaining > 0 do
    task.wait()
end

Both examples produce the same results, but the concurrent version allows the engine to automatically batch multiple API calls into fewer HTTP requests, making the operation faster and reducing the likelihood of hitting rate limits.

Supported methods

The following methods currently support transparent batching:

Service Method
Class.MarketplaceService Class.MarketplaceService:GetProductInfoAsync()|GetProductInfoAsync (Enum.InfoType.Product, Enum.InfoType.GamePass, and Enum.InfoType.Bundle)
Class.MarketplaceService Class.MarketplaceService:UserOwnsGamePassAsync()|UserOwnsGamePassAsync
Class.AvatarEditorService Class.AvatarEditorService:GetItemDetailsAsync()|GetItemDetailsAsync
Class.AssetService Class.AssetService:GetBundleDetailsAsync()|GetBundleDetailsAsync

Best practices

  • Start calls close together. The engine batches calls that begin within a short time window. Calls started much later are sent in a separate batch.
  • Use pcall(). Network requests can fail. Wrapping calls in pcall() prevents a single failure from stopping the entire operation.
  • Let the engine manage batching. Don't try to manually group requests or optimize batch sizes. The engine automatically chooses the most efficient batching strategy.
  • Take advantage of caching. Repeated requests for the same data return from cache whenever possible instead of making another network request.

kid.simple: Some Roblox functions have to ask Roblox's servers on the internet for information, like the price of a product. If you ask many questions at the same time, Roblox can quietly bundle them into just a few trips instead of one trip per question. This is called transparent batching. You get it for free, as long as you start your calls at the same time instead of one after another.
kid.analogy: If you need 20 things from the store, it is much faster to go once with a full shopping list than to drive there 20 times for one item each. Starting your requests together lets Roblox make one trip with a list.
keyPoints: Transparent batching means the engine combines many calls to the same API into fewer internet requests for you.
You do not need a special function or extra settings. You just start the calls at the same time.
If each call waits for the last one to finish, nothing gets batched and every call makes its own request.
Use `task.spawn` to start several calls at once.
Fewer requests means faster results and less chance of hitting rate limits.
Wrap each call in `pcall` because internet requests can fail.
Do not try to group requests yourself. Let the engine pick the best batch size.

terms.HTTP request: A message your game sends over the internet to a Roblox server to ask for or send information.
terms.batching: Grouping many small jobs into one bigger job. 20 product lookups might become just 1 or 2 requests.
terms.transparent: Here it means it happens automatically behind the scenes, so you do not have to see or manage it.
terms.concurrent: Happening at the same time. Five concurrent calls are all started together, not one after another.
terms.serial: One after another. Each call waits for the previous one to finish before starting.
terms.rate limit: A cap on how many requests you can make in a short time. Go over it and some requests slow down or fail.
terms.latency: The delay between asking for something and getting the answer.
terms.throttled: Slowed down or blocked because too many requests were sent too fast.
terms.pcall: Short for protected call. It runs a function and catches errors so one failure does not crash your whole script.
terms.cache: A saved copy of an earlier answer, so asking again can skip the internet trip.

example.title: Look up several products at once
example.code:
local MarketplaceService = game:GetService("MarketplaceService")

-- Replace these with your own developer product IDs
local productIds = { 1111111, 2222222, 3333333 }

local results = {}
local remaining = #productIds

local function fetch(productId)
	-- pcall catches errors so one bad lookup does not stop the rest
	local success, info = pcall(function()
		return MarketplaceService:GetProductInfoAsync(productId, Enum.InfoType.Product)
	end)
	if success then
		results[productId] = info
	else
		warn("Failed:", productId, info)
	end
	remaining -= 1
end

-- Start every lookup at the same time so the engine can batch them
for _, productId in productIds do
	task.spawn(fetch, productId)
end

-- Wait until all lookups have finished
while remaining > 0 do
	task.wait()
end

for id, info in results do
	print(id, info.Name)
end
explain: `productIds` is the list of products you want to know about.
`remaining` counts how many lookups are still running.
`fetch` asks for one product's info inside `pcall`, saves it, and lowers the counter by 1.
`task.spawn(fetch, productId)` starts every lookup right away, all together, so Roblox can bundle them.
The `while` loop waits a frame at a time until `remaining` reaches 0.
Finally, the script prints each product's name.

watchOut: Calling the API inside a plain `for` loop. Each call waits for the last, so nothing batches. Use `task.spawn` for each call.
Forgetting `pcall`. One failed request can stop your whole script without it.
Starting calls far apart in time. Only calls that start close together get batched.
Expecting every API to batch. Only the methods listed on the page support it.
